newsitem.title: UK: P&O aims to float Bovis Homes in Sept or Oct.
newsitem.headline: P&O aims to float Bovis Homes in Sept or Oct.

text.p: Shipping to construction group The Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co (P&O) said on Tuesday it planned to go ahead with the flotation of its Bovis Homes unit in September or October.
Chairman Lord Sterling dismissed a report by a Sunday newspaper that the group had been forced to postpone the float of its British housebuilding unit.
"Unless the (financial) markets fall out of bed...we will be floating in the late autumn," he told Reuters.

He said 100 percent of the company would be sold off. P&O said in its annual results released earlier that Bovis Homes made a 68 percent increase in its operating profits last year to 28.8 million stg on net operating assets of 232 million stg. Sales rose 25.3 million stg to 292.2 million.

Sterling said the current year had started well but it was decided to leave the flotation until either September or more likely October to get the benefits of the current revival in demand for new homes in Britain.
"They (Bovis Homes) have really got their act together. It's carrying through strongly and it will obviously be in the interest of shareholders to float it in late autumn," he said.
"One would be able to talk then quite strongly about what it is doing in '97."
